conclusions: SHA512/MD5 streaming buffer publication and logical mapping separation are useful design references. Existing SHA512 metadata reused without fresh byte comparison; no actual hash collision demonstrated. Content type is associated with hash rather than each logical mapping.

Cleanup selects orphan hashes and acquires advisory locks in one query, then deletes physical objects before metadata deletion rechecks mappings. Possible stale-selection race when waiting for a writer remains source-only and unconfirmed.

Seven named PostgreSQL integration tests fully read. Dangling-lock test starts cleanup first, then writer; it does not reproduce writer-first stale selection or physical backend deletion. Metadata size retention on conflict is explicitly expected by a test.
No explicit transaction spans backend object publication, metadata and logical mapping. No executed crash recovery, concurrency, backend partial-deletion or real storage integrity qualification.

Docker runtime stage installs CA certificates and Java25 but not curl; curl installation is confined to build stage while runtime HEALTHCHECK calls curl. Healthcheck also requests root path, whereas application routes are /proxy/ and /api/ with unmatched routes returning404. Static observations, not a built container result.
Release workflow invokes sbt stage and publishes artifacts/images, with no sbt test step. Packaging is not evidence of passing tests. No workflow, deployment or publishing executed.
